title: 1972 AHSME Problem 16
statement: There are two positive numbers that may be inserted between \(3\) and \(9\) such that the first three are in geometric progression while the last three are in arithmetic progression. The sum of those two positive numbers is:

solutions.text:
The progression conditions give \(x^2=3y\) and \(2y=x+9.\) Eliminating \(y\) yields \[ \begin{aligned} 2x^2-3x-27&=(2x-9)(x+3)\\ &=0. \end{aligned} \] Positivity gives \(x=\frac{9}{2},\) and then \(y=\frac{27}{4}.\) Their sum is \[ \frac92+\frac{27}{4}=\frac{45}{4}=11\frac14. \]

Therefore, the correct answer is B.
hints: Call the inserted numbers \(x\) and \(y,\) in that order
